entry.title: Touying 0.8.0
entry.summary: Touying 0.8.0 is a big release, and the first that requires Typst 0.15. The headline feature is article mode: one source file compiles either to slides or to a flowing prose document. And we have two new animation functions.
entry.content:
Touying 0.8.0 is a big release, and the first that requires Typst 0.15. The headline feature is article mode: one source file compiles either to slides or to a flowing prose document. And we have two new animation functions.

Article mode​

A handout deck written for projection rarely reads well as a prose document, and a document written for reading rarely projects well. Article mode lets one file be both. Compile with --input export-mode=article and the deck becomes a continuous document: no slide breaks, animations collapsed to their final state, images optionally floated to the side.

The interesting part is what happens where the two outputs should differ. #article-text[..] replaces the body of the slide it is written in, so a slide of bullet points can become a paragraph of prose:

== Results
- First point
- Second point

#article-text[
  In the article this slide becomes a prose paragraph instead of bullets.
]

#article-only[..] and #slides-only[..] restrict content to one output, and config-article(..) covers the article side of the layout: wrap floats elements beside the text, linearize decides how much of the deck's structure comes apart — a composer's columns become flowing text, while a table with a header keeps its shape — and #article-linearize[..] / #article-keep-layout[..] override that per element. See Article Mode.

Two new animation functions​

#animate layers several effects on one piece of content, each over its own subslide range. A placement ("show", "cover", "remove" or swap(..)) decides whether the body appears; a styling function wraps whatever the placement left:

#animate(
  [Photosynthesis],
  effects: (
    (effect: swap([Respiration], stretch: true), subslides: "2-"),
    (effect: (body, self: none) => text(fill: red, body), subslides: "3-"),
  ),
)

#touying-render takes content held in a variable and renders it at a chosen stage, so an animated element can be shown mid-animation without writing it out again:

#let steps = [A #pause B #pause C]
#touying-render(steps, subslides: 2)

#touying-recall was extended from whole slides to any labelled element, and a #slide[..] can carry a label of its own, so several slides under one heading stay individually addressable.

Animations inside math​

#pause, #uncover, #only and #alternatives now work inside the math elements that keep their content in named fields — frac, mat, vec, cases, binom, root, attach, accent and the brace family. These used to abort the compile with Unsupported mark:

$ frac(a #pause + b, c) $

touying-equation is deprecated as a result; plain math is more capable than it ever was.

Things to watch when upgrading​

  • Typst 0.15 is required.
  • A #pause after uncover/only/alternatives no longer skips the subslides they reserve. v0.7.0 made a relative jump snap past any preceding wrapper, which was meant for item-by-item but caught the others too. If you relied on it, add the #pause yourself.
  • show-bibliography-as-footnote is a boolean now, and magic.bibliography() is gone — set the flag and put a real #bibliography(..) in the presentation.
  • semi-transparent-cover is deprecated in favour of alpha-changing-cover and color-changing-cover.
  • The speaker-note panel is a theme-supplied function via config-common(notes-fn: ..); the config-methods(show-only-notes: ..) renderer is gone.

The changelog has a full migration guide, and a separate one for theme authors at the end.

Also new​

  • .pdfpc files as bundle assets, written directly instead of through a separate typst query step.
  • touying-fn-wrapper-raw parses and nests its body, so #alert[.. #pause ..] works.
  • Overflow detection checks width as well as height, and detect-overflow defaults to auto, following breakable.
  • Internally, src/core.typ (6288 lines) was split into modules and the content handling was unified — most documentation pages were rewritten or corrected alongside it.

entry.title: Touying 0.7.4
entry.summary: Touying 0.7.4 adds on-slide navigation arrows, easier integration with external packages, and a batch of fixes around warnings.
entry.content:
Touying 0.7.4 adds on-slide navigation arrows, easier integration with external packages, and a batch of fixes around warnings.

What's New​

  • lr-navigation: a navigation element with links to the previous and next subslide or slide, plus a centre icon (#352). Put it in a footer and the arrows become clickable links in the exported PDF; mode chooses between "subslide", "page" and "both", and show-useless: false hides links that would go nowhere. You can choose custom icons.
#lr-navigation(mode: "both", show-useless: false)
  • touying-reduce: automatically looks up reducer bindings for a given package (#363), so integrating an external package's functions with Touying's animations takes less setup.
  • components.full-width-block: a block that spans the full page width by cancelling the horizontal margins.
  • lazy-layout gained a grid-size parameter for quantized position grouping, making column and row detection more robust.
  • Polish locale for the outline message (#372).

Fixes​

  • Minor breaking change: the lazy-layout parameter of cols now defaults to false instead of true, so columns are no longer height-equalised unless you ask.
  • hide no longer does unexpected things to headings (#366).
  • touying-fn-wrapper-raw is now exported as part of the public API (#362).
  • Mark warnings are improved and are also shown as magic.warning when enable-mark-warning is false (#348); a missing fn field in a mark warning message is handled gracefully.
  • Warnings are now emitted via uniwarn (#359).

entry.title: Touying 0.7.3
entry.summary: Touying 0.7.3 fixes a long-standing speaker-note pitfall — at the cost of two small breaking changes — and adds more control over item-by-item animations and progressive outlines.
entry.content:
Touying 0.7.3 fixes a long-standing speaker-note pitfall — at the cost of two small breaking changes — and adds more control over item-by-item animations and progressive outlines.

Minor Breaking Changes​

#speaker-note[] now always attaches to the slide above it (#354), no matter how that slide was created: an explicit slide call, a heading-triggered section slide, or a normal content slide. This gets rid of the common pitfall where a #speaker-note[] placed after a slide silently created an unwanted empty "ghost" slide.

Along with it, receive-body-for-new-section-slide-fn and its variants now default to false (previously true). If you relied on content after a = Section heading being absorbed into the section slide body, set it explicitly:

#import "@preview/touying:0.7.3": *
#import themes.university: *

#show: university-theme.with(
  config-common(receive-body-for-new-section-slide-fn: true),
)

What's New​

  • item-by-item-fn and presets for it (#347).
  • Progressive outlines: custom-progressive-outline was improved, and there is a new section-relationship (#345).
  • cols: a new alias of side-by-side, with cols and the lazy-* components now exported (#356). lazy-layout also handles mixed layouts better (#355).
  • Metropolis gained an outline slide (#349).
  • A warning is now emitted when an empty slide content height is detected.

entry.title: Touying 0.7.1
entry.summary: Touying 0.7.1 is a small follow-up release, focused on keeping content inside the slide it belongs to.
entry.content:
Touying 0.7.1 is a small follow-up release, focused on keeping content inside the slide it belongs to.

What's New​

  • Overflow handling: breakable and clip options to avoid slide overflow (#336). With breakable: false a slide is constrained to a single page instead of spilling onto a new one, and clip decides whether the excess is truncated or merely left to overhang.
  • lazy-layout: new lazy-v and lazy-h components, plus lazy-layout, for equalising the heights of multiple columns (or the widths of multiple rows) (#339).
  • More title metadata: config-info gained contact and extra fields (#342). extra takes a dict that a theme reads back as self.info.extra.key.
  • touying-get-config: a function for reading the current configuration (#333).

Fixes​

  • fit-to-height and size-to-pt are fixed, and text is allowed to reflow (#332).
  • Waypoint markers are fixed (#341).

entry.title: Touying 0.7.0
entry.summary: Touying 0.7.0 is a large release built around one major feature — named waypoints — together with a long list of animation and layout fixes.
entry.content:
Touying 0.7.0 is a large release built around one major feature — named waypoints — together with a long list of animation and layout fixes.

Named waypoints​

Animations have always been addressed by subslide number, which means counting #pausees by hand and renumbering everything whenever you insert one. Named waypoints (#298, by @zral0kh) let you name a position in the animation instead.

#waypoint(<label>) marks a spot — and, like #pause, advances to the next subslide unless you pass advance: false. A waypoint covers every subslide from its declaration until the next waypoint or the end of the slide, so passing the label to uncover, only, effect or alternatives shows content for exactly that stretch. Two markers turn a waypoint into an open range: from-wp is visible from it onwards, until-wp up to just before it. Labels need only be unique within a single slide, and they may be referenced before they are declared.

#uncover(until-wp(<summary>))[Shown before the summary.]

Main content.

#waypoint(<summary>)

Summary text. #pause More summary.

#uncover(from-wp(<summary>))[Visible from the summary on.]

That is three subslides: the first shows the intro line and the main content, the second swaps it for the summary, the third adds the rest — and nothing had to be numbered. get-first and get-last pick out a single edge of a waypoint, prev-wp and next-wp shift a reference by whole waypoints, and hierarchical labels such as <part:intro> are combined when you refer to <part>. The start parameter sets where a waypoint begins independently of where it sits in the content (#304), and waypoints work in handout-subslides too.

Also new​

  • More flexible subslide numbers: specifications now accept auto and the "h" ("here") string, with an inverse function for string subslide numbers and waypoints (#301).
  • Animation functions via reducer: functions based on fn-wrapper are now implicitly allowed through the reducer (#300), making custom animation helpers easier to build.

Fixes​

  • Covers: cover-with-rect no longer breaks long lines of text when they are partially hidden, and colour and alpha covers gained fallback functions (#328). Cover spacing around lists was also fixed (#303).
  • Show rules: ghost slides caused by show rules are gone, and show rules and the defer keyword are handled consistently (#317).
  • Headings: display-current-heading uses explicit numbering when style: auto (#329).
  • Layout: alternatives-match respects stretch (#320), and page margin merging and precedence are correct (#322).
  • Plus alert no longer delayed (#316), negative subslide indices parsed correctly for handout-subslides (#307), and slide updating via a scoped import (#310).

Thanks for the contributions from @zral0kh, @Andrew15-5, @navdeeprana, and @Cemoixerestre.

entry.title: Touying 0.6.3
entry.summary: Touying 0.6.3 is a major bugfix release that also brings a batch of practical new features, most of them around animations and handout mode.
entry.content:
Touying 0.6.3 is a major bugfix release that also brings a batch of practical new features, most of them around animations and handout mode.

What's New​

  • #jump as unified animation control: #jump(n, relative: false) is the new primitive for moving the subslide counter, and #pause and #meanwhile are now sugar on top of it. #jump(3) skips straight to subslide 3.
  • #item-by-item reveals a list, enum or terms block one item at a time (#278):
#item-by-item[
  - First
  - Second
  - Third
]
  • #touying-raw reveals a code block progressively, splitting on a pause comment in the code itself (#283):
#touying-raw(```rust
fn main() {
    // pause
    println!("Hello, world!");
}
```)
  • Handout mode, more precisely: #handout-only[..] marks inline content as handout-exclusive and the <touying:handout> label does the same for a whole slide (#286), while handout-subslides picks which subslides survive (#288).
  • Speaker notes and aspect ratios: a full-screen notes mode with a slide thumbnail via show-only-notes (#281), and arbitrary aspect ratios such as 16-10 across all themes (#280).
  • Also: a subslide parameter for #touying-recall (#285), default-composer in config-common for a global slide layout (#284), a cover-fn parameter on uncover for packages like Fletcher (#267), and inline minislides (#228).

Fixes​

Many long-standing bugs are gone: ghost blank slides from a touying-set-config anchor regression, styled content on the first slide creating extra slides, #meanwhile being ignored inside grid cells and boxes, the config: parameter being silently ignored across all themes, and slides after #show/#set rules not rendering. See the Changelog for the full list.

For theme authors​

Move config to the last position in utils.merge-dicts so user overrides win, and replace paper with utils.page-args-from-aspect-ratio to support arbitrary aspect ratios:

self = utils.merge-dicts(self, config-page(..utils.page-args-from-aspect-ratio(aspect-ratio), ...), config)

The documentation website was also substantially restructured in this release, with a new references page and docstrings across all source files.

entry.title: Touying 0.6.2
entry.summary: Touying 0.6.2 is a small maintenance release, mostly about getting Touying working smoothly on Typst 0.14.
entry.content:
Touying 0.6.2 is a small maintenance release, mostly about getting Touying working smoothly on Typst 0.14.

What's New​

  • Typst 0.14 compatibility: fixed magic.bibliography-as-footnote (#249) and the breakage of the theorion package on Typst 0.14.0 (#237).
  • Customisable checkerboard: components.checkerboard now takes columns, rows, alignment, primary and secondary (#161).
  • Full-width headers: ratio and relative margins are now supported (#256).
  • #meanwhile in CeTZ: fixed (#205).

Plus a handful of smaller fixes: the correct circle symbol, equation colour overrides via regex, show-hide-set-list-marker-none with a full enum, and better caching after removing the dump and label-it helpers.

entry.title: Touying 0.6.1
entry.summary: Touying 0.6.1 adds first-class support for the theorion package and uses it as the default math theorem environment.
entry.content:
Touying 0.6.1 adds first-class support for the theorion package and uses it as the default math theorem environment.

What's New​

  • Theorion integration: Added built-in support for the theorion package, which provides beautiful numbered theorem, lemma, corollary, definition, and proof environments. It is now the recommended way to write theorem blocks in Touying slides.
#import "@preview/touying:0.6.1": *
#import themes.university: *
#import "@preview/theorion:0.3.2": *
#import cosmos.clouds: *
#show: show-theorion

#show: university-theme.with(
  aspect-ratio: "16-9",
  config-common(frozen-counters: (theorem-counter,)),
)

= Theorems

== Prime numbers

#theorem(title: "Euclid")[
  There are infinitely many primes.
]

See the Theorion integration guide for more details.

entry.title: Touying 0.6.0
entry.summary: Touying 0.6.0 is the first release since Typst 0.13 and brings several quality-of-life improvements.
entry.content:
Touying 0.6.0 is the first release since Typst 0.13 and brings several quality-of-life improvements.

Features​

  • Auto heading style: utils.display-current-heading(level: 1, style: auto) now respects show rules like show heading: set text(blue).
  • Document metadata: config-info fields are now applied to set document automatically.
  • alternatives default: stretch: false is now the default — content no longer expands to fill the slide automatically. (Minor breaking change — more intuitive behaviour.)

Fixes​

  • Fix error with uncover using semi-transparent-cover.
  • Fix type string comparison (#153).
  • Fix horizontal-line bug in Typst 0.13.0.
  • Refactor: fix display-current-short-heading.

Getting Started​

#import "@preview/touying:0.6.1": *
#import themes.university: *

#show: university-theme.with(
  aspect-ratio: "16-9",
  config-info(
    title: [My Talk],
    author: [Alice],
    date: datetime.today(),
  ),
)

#title-slide()

= Introduction

== Hello

#lorem(40)

entry.title: Touying 0.5.0 — A Major Redesign
entry.summary: Touying 0.5.0 is a significant rewrite. The goal: make Touying more user-friendly, more flexible, and more powerful.
entry.content:
Touying 0.5.0 is a significant rewrite. The goal: make Touying more user-friendly, more flexible, and more powerful.

Major Changes​

No more closures — cleaner config syntax​

Configuration is now done with config-xxx functions:

#show: university-theme.with(
  aspect-ratio: "16-9",
  config-colors(primary: blue),
  config-info(title: [My Talk], author: [Alice]),
)

New Stargazer theme​

A new visually striking theme, originally created by Coekjan for the touying-buaa project.

Fake frozen states​

Use numbering and #pause together without issues. Control with config-common(frozen-counters: ...).

Special heading labels​

<touying:hidden>, <touying:unnumbered>, <touying:unoutlined>, <touying:unbookmarked> for precise control over heading behaviour.

#show: appendix​

Freeze the slide counter at the end of your main content:

#show: appendix

= Appendix

== Extra Slide

Please pay attention to the current slide number.

Adaptive columns for outlines​

#components.adaptive-columns(outline(indent: 1em))

Migration Guide​

See the Changelog for the detailed step-by-step migration guide from 0.4.x.

entry.title: Touying 0.2.0
entry.content:
Touying 0.2.0 is done.

Implemented Features​

  • Object-oriented programming: Singleton s, binding methods utils.methods(s) and (self: obj, ..) => {..} methods.
  • Page arguments management: Instead of using #set page(..), you should use self.page-args to retrieve or set page parameters, thereby avoiding unnecessary creation of new pages.
  • #pause for sequence content: You can use #pause at the outermost level of a slide, including inline and list.
  • #pause for layout functions: You can use the composer parameter to add yourself layout function like utils.side-by-side, and simply use multiple pos parameters like #slide[..][..].
  • #meanwhile for synchronous display: Provide a #meanwhile for resetting subslides counter.
  • #pause and #meanwhile for math equation: Provide a #touying-equation("x + y pause + z") for math equation animations.
  • Slides: Create simple slides using standard headings.
  • Callback-style uncover, only and alternatives: Based on the concise syntax provided by Polylux, allow precise control of the timing for displaying content.
    • You should manually control the number of subslides using the repeat parameter.
  • Transparent cover: Enable transparent cover using oop syntax like #let s = (s.methods.enable-transparent-cover)(self: s).
  • Handout mode: enable handout mode by #let s = (s.methods.enable-handout-mode)(self: s).
  • Fit-to-width and fit-to-height: Fit-to-width for title in header and fit-to-height for image.
    • utils.fit-to-width(grow: true, shrink: true, width, body)
    • utils.fit-to-height(width: none, prescale-width: none, grow: true, shrink: true, height, body)
  • Slides counter: states.slide-counter.display() + " / " + states.last-slide-number and states.touying-progress(ratio => ..).
  • Appendix: Freeze the last-slide-number to prevent the slide number from increasing further.
  • Sections: Touying's built-in section support can be used to display the current section title and show progress.
    • section and subsection parameter in #slide to register a new section or subsection.
    • states.current-section-title to get the current section.
    • states.touying-outline or s.methods.touying-outline to display a outline of sections.
    • states.touying-final-sections(sections => ..) for custom outline display.
    • states.touying-progress-with-sections((current-sections: .., final-sections: .., current-slide-number: .., last-slide-number: ..) => ..) for powerful progress display.
  • Navigation bar: Navigation bar like here by states.touying-progress-with-sections(..), in dewdrop theme.
  • Pdfpc: pdfpc support and export .pdfpc file without external tool by typst query command simply.
